svg.title: CPU datapath: instruction fetch, asynchronous register read, execution, and synchronous register write
svg.desc: Read left to right. Instruction memory supplies the frontend and one execution slot. Decode selects two asynchronous register-file read ports. ALU, branch, multiply, divide, and load-store units feed the writeback mux, then the synchronous register-file write port. The register read and write boxes are two views of one physical 32-register file, not separate banks. Data memory sits below the load-store unit with vertical request and response arrows. Instruction and data memory boxes are the two logical ports of one physical RAM. The frontend includes one existing clocked response buffer and a combinational bypass for a fresh response. Border clock wedges mark positive-edge state or enabled writes; pure combinational blocks have no wedge. RAM wedges refer to their clocked port model. The layout groups functions, not RTL modules. Fetch overlaps one serialized backend, not five independently occupied pipeline stages.
svg.text: Functional datapath · one serialized backend slot
The frontend belongs to teaching_fetch; execution functions belong to teaching_backend. The shaded area is not a module boundary.
One physical RAM · two logical I / D ports
Dashed links identify a shared resource; they are not data paths.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_fetch : teaching_fetch. next_pc is a positive-edge register output Q, not a combinational next-state wire. The request-address mux selects held_pc when held, otherwise next_pc. The displayed value is req_addr, not an observation of next_pc. See the PC-path inset below.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_fetch : teaching_fetch. next_pc is a positive-edge register output Q, not a combinational next-state wire. The request-address mux selects held_pc when held, otherwise next_pc. The displayed value is req_addr, not an observation of next_pc. See the PC-path inset below.

g.aria-label: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, instruction port. One external shared RAM model. Request tracking and response outputs update on the positive edge. The marker describes the clocked port model; it does not claim the RAM array is made from flip-flops.
g.title: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, instruction port. One external shared RAM model. Request tracking and response outputs update on the positive edge. The marker describes the clocked port model; it does not claim the RAM array is made from flip-flops.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_fetch : teaching_fetch. Functional view of the existing one-entry buffer and combinational fresh-response bypass. The complete delivery box is not a register or an unimplemented queue; only the buffer subblock carries a clock marker.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_fetch : teaching_fetch. Functional view of the existing one-entry buffer and combinational fresh-response bypass. The complete delivery box is not a register or an unimplemented queue; only the buffer subblock carries a clock marker.
Existing one-entry response buffer in teaching_fetch: buf_pc, buf_insn, buf_valid, buf_fault, and buf_misaligned. It captures an unconsumed fresh response at the rising edge.

Combinational output selection: use the valid buffered word, otherwise the fresh accepted response. A fresh response can enter the instruction slot at this same edge without first occupying the response buffer.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend : teaching_backend. Inline positive-edge registers pc_pipe_r, insn_pipe_r, valid_pipe_r, and fetch-fault metadata. This is not a separate instantiated module.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend : teaching_backend. Inline positive-edge registers pc_pipe_r, insn_pipe_r, valid_pipe_r, and fetch-fault metadata. This is not a separate instantiated module.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_decoder : rv32_decoder. Combinational decode, with additional encoding_legal filtering in teaching_backend. No clocked decode stage.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_decoder : rv32_decoder. Combinational decode, with additional encoding_legal filtering in teaching_backend. No clocked decode stage.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf, SYNC_READ=0, WB_FORWARD=0. Two asynchronous read ports of the same register file shown at the right. No read register.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf, SYNC_READ=0, WB_FORWARD=0. Two asynchronous read ports of the same register file shown at the right. No read register.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_alu : fu_alu, plus combinational operand selection and u_alu_op : rv32_alu_op_decode. The ALU has protocol clock pins but no edge-triggered datapath state in this configuration.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_alu : fu_alu, plus combinational operand selection and u_alu_op : rv32_alu_op_decode. The ALU has protocol clock pins but no edge-triggered datapath state in this configuration.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_br : fu_br. Combinational comparison, branch target, and jump-link result. Redirect and trap priority are selected in teaching_backend.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_br : fu_br. Combinational comparison, branch target, and jump-link result. Redirect and trap priority are selected in teaching_backend.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_mul : fu_mul, MUL_L=1. Combinational multiplication followed by positive-edge product, operation, valid, and tag state.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_mul : fu_mul, MUL_L=1. Combinational multiplication followed by positive-edge product, operation, valid, and tag state.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_div : fu_div. Positive-edge iterative state, accumulator, divisor, sign, operation, and counter registers. The backend also holds its instruction and wait counter.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_div : fu_div. Positive-edge iterative state, accumulator, divisor, sign, operation, and counter registers. The backend also holds its instruction and wait counter.

g.aria-label: Functional group in teaching_backend, not a standalone LSU module: address from the shared u_alu; clocked execution substate and load_data_r plus combinational u_ls_split : rv32_ls_split and u_ls_align2 : rv32_ls_align2. The clock marker applies to response/control state, not to the byte-lane logic.
g.title: Functional group in teaching_backend, not a standalone LSU module: address from the shared u_alu; clocked execution substate and load_data_r plus combinational u_ls_split : rv32_ls_split and u_ls_align2 : rv32_ls_align2. The clock marker applies to response/control state, not to the byte-lane logic.

g.aria-label: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, data port of the same RAM as the I port. Request tracking, responses, and enabled memory writes are positive-edge operations. This is not a second RAM instance or an all-flop SRAM claim.
g.title: tb_cpu_lab.u_mem : teaching_sram, data port of the same RAM as the I port. Request tracking, responses, and enabled memory writes are positive-edge operations. This is not a second RAM instance or an all-flop SRAM claim.

g.aria-label: Inline always_comb result mux in teaching_backend. Selects the final result for the RF write port. No independent register, no extra pipeline stage, and no clock marker.
g.title: Inline always_comb result mux in teaching_backend. Selects the final result for the RF write port. No independent register, no extra pipeline stage, and no clock marker.

g.aria-label: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf. One positive-edge write port, enabled only by wb_en and a nonzero destination. This is the same physical RF as the left read view.
g.title: teaching_cpu.u_backend.u_rf : rv32_rf. One positive-edge write port, enabled only by wb_en and a nonzero destination. This is the same physical RF as the left read view.

svg.text: Register operands, immediates and PC feed the selected unit.
Clock wedge = positive-edge stored state or enabled write. RAM wedges mark the clocked interface/model, not an all-flop array.
Memory transfers occur on valid AND ready. Solid highlighted arrows mark accepted transfers; dashed amber arrows mark offered transfers waiting.
Highlights show logical activity in the selected trace sample, not physical switching. A register write occurs only when its recorded write enable is asserted.

g.title: Actual fetch PC registers and request-address selection
g.desc: This static expansion explains the fetch-control box above; it does not depict additional module instances or sampled internal register values. next_pc is a clocked register Q. The combinational request mux selects held_pc or next_pc and drives instruction-memory req_addr. On request acceptance, pending_pc captures that same address. The next_pc register instead takes redirect_pc with priority, or req_addr plus four for an accepted non-obsolete request, or holds its previous value. held_pc captures an offered request when ready is low. pending_pc follows the response into the existing buffer or fresh bypass and finally the backend PC register on admission.
g.text: Inside fetch control: the PC register is before the request-address mux
Static RTL expansion · these labels identify signals and registers, not additional live values or separate pipeline stages.
req_addr + 4, enabled only by a live request acceptance
Existing delivery path: buffered buf_pc or fresh pending_pc
Response PC and instruction bits stay associated through waits and redirects.
An obsolete held request still completes;
it does not advance the redirected PC.
SRAM receives req_addr. pending_pc captures that address; next_pc instead receives the selected next-state value.
Despite its name, next_pc is registered Q. There is no separate signal named pc_nxt in this RTL; the selection above is implicit in always_ff.
